prompt: Let $P,Q,R$ be classical propositions; $\top$ means true, $\bot$ means false, and $\equiv$ means equal truth values under every assignment. Which identity is the standard commutative law for conjunction?

answers.explanation: The two operands exchange places while the connective stays the same.
This is double negation (involution). Applying negation twice restores the original truth value.
This is de morgan’s law. Moving negation through a conjunction negates both operands and changes conjunction to disjunction.
This is complement law (excluded middle). A proposition and its negation cover both possible truth values.
This is identity law (neutral element). A neutral constant leaves the other operand unchanged.
This is domination law (absorbing element). An absorbing constant fixes the result regardless of the other operand.
This is idempotence. Combining a proposition with itself using conjunction adds no new requirement.
This is associativity. Only the grouping changes; the order of the operands and the connective stay fixed.
This is distributivity. Disjunction distributes over conjunction, repeating the outside operand in both resulting disjunctions.
This is absorption. The conjunction can only be true when the repeated proposition already makes the outer disjunction true.

sources.title: Martin J. Dürst — Discrete Mathematics I: Laws for Logical Operations
